intro: A flat described in a text of about 170 words with twelve adjectives to complete — spread across all three tables you have just learnt. After der-words: Das große Wohnzimmer, auf dem bequemen Sofa, der junge Mann. After ein-words: in einer neuen Wohnung, ein großes Fenster, einen kleinen Park, ein schönes Bild, einen neuen Herd, einen modernen Kühlschrank, ein alter Baum. With no article at all (a preview of the Nullartikel): nette Nachbarn, mit heißem Tee. Each gap gives you only the adjective. Work through it with the three questions in order: which article (der-word, ein-word, none)? which gender and number? which case? — then read the ending off the table. This is the habit that makes endings reliable: no guessing, three questions.
tips[0].title: Three questions per gap
tips[0].text: 1. What is before the adjective — a der-word, an ein-word or nothing? 2. What gender and number is the noun? 3. What case does the sentence put it in (subject, object, after a preposition)? Then the ending is fixed.
tips[0].check.why: ein-word, neuter, dative after in (where?) → einem, and in the dative the adjective takes -en.
tips[0].visual.caption: Ask the three questions in this order for every gap.
tips[0].visual.moves[0].label: Which case?
tips[0].visual.moves[1].label: Which gender and number?
tips[0].visual.moves[2].label: Does the article already show it?
tips[1].title: Prepositions decide the case first
tips[1].text: auf dem Sofa, vor dem Haus, in einer Wohnung, mit Tee: positions and mit take the dative, and the dative makes the adjective -en after any article. Two rules stack: first the case from the preposition, then the ending from the case.
tips[1].trap: English adjectives never change, so the ending is easy to forget once the preposition has taken your attention. Say the whole phrase aloud: in einer neuen Wohnung.
tips[1].check.why: unter + where? takes the dative: dem, and after dem the adjective ends in -en.
tips[2].title: No article? The adjective takes the der-ending
tips[2].text: Ich habe nette Nachbarn — no article, plural accusative → the adjective wears the die-ending: -e. mit heißem Tee — no article, masculine dative → the dem-ending: -em. The full Nullartikel table is the next-but-one quiz.
tips[2].check.why: No article, masculine dative after mit: the adjective takes the dem-ending, -em.
remember[0]: Article type → gender/number → case → ending. Always in that order.
remember[1]: Dative after an article = -en; dative with no article = -em / -er / -en.
hook: Describe a flat in German, from the sofa and the big window to the old tree outside, with every adjective ending right and no guessing.
